incumbent.name: Martin Carbaugh
incumbent.summary: Martin Carbaugh, a Fort Wayne financial planner, has represented House District 81 since 2012 and chairs the House Insurance Committee {caucus_carbaugh} {wiki_2026}. He authored the 2025 law (HEA 1004) setting price benchmarks for large nonprofit hospital systems {wpta_hea1004}.
record: Committees: Insurance (chair), Education and Public Health; interim committees on Financial Institutions and Insurance and on Pension Management Oversight, according to the House Republican caucus {caucus_carbaugh}.

2025: Authored HEA 1004, which requires the largest nonprofit hospital systems to bring average prices to or below a statewide average by June 30, 2029, or risk losing nonprofit status {wpta_hea1004}. Carbaugh said at final passage: "Even with those changes, we are making meaningful, incremental changes to provide relief to our constituents" {icc_hea1004}.

HEA 1004 criticism: Rep. Robin Shackleford (D-Indianapolis) said "There is nothing in this bill that ensures that patients will pay less for quality health care"; Sen. Liz Brown (R-Fort Wayne) warned that loss of nonprofit status could lead to sales of facilities that leave out rural hospitals {icc_hea1004}. In April 2026 Carbaugh said large nonprofit hospitals were complying with the law's direct-to-employer provisions but that marketplace and other insured patients still need help {caucus_hospital_2026}.

2026: Sponsored SEA 88, which adds instruction on finishing high school, workforce training, full-time employment and waiting to become a parent until marriage to existing coursework, and recognizes the Classic Learning Test as a college entrance exam {caucus_sea88}.

Voted yes on SEA 1, the 2025 property-tax law (April 10, 2025) {rc_sea1_433}; the 2025 budget conference report, HEA 1001 (April 25, 2025) {rc_hb1001_576}; and HB 1032, the congressional redistricting bill (Dec. 5, 2025) {rc_hb1032_28}.

race_context: House District 81 covers the northwestern part of Fort Wayne and part of central Allen County, according to the House Republican caucus {caucus_carbaugh}; the Journal Gazette describes it as including northwest Allen County {jg_d81}. Wight cites growth in Huntertown as a district issue {jg_d81}.
Carbaugh was reelected with 64.9% of the vote in 2024 {wiki_2026}.
May 5, 2026 Republican primary: Carbaugh 3,795 votes (75.1%), David Mervar 1,256 (24.9%). Democratic primary: Sharon Wight 1,976 (81.6%), Chad Clevidence 446 (18.4%) {wiki_2026}.

Key differences: Carbaugh's legislative focus has been health care pricing and insurance {caucus_carbaugh} {caucus_hospital_2026}; Wight emphasizes accessibility, public transit, public-school funding, union support and marijuana legalization {wight_platform}.
No debate or forum for this race was found.

candidates.summary: Seven-term incumbent and chair of the House Insurance Committee {caucus_carbaugh}. Won the May 2026 Republican primary with 75.1% {wiki_2026}.
background: Financial planner with Financial Focus; attended Indiana University-Purdue University Fort Wayne; lifelong Fort Wayne resident {caucus_carbaugh}.

Volunteers with Junior Achievement teaching financial literacy; member of the National Association of Insurance and Financial Advisors and the National Federation of Independent Business {caucus_carbaugh}.
path_to_ballot: Won the May 5, 2026 Republican primary over David Mervar, 75.1% to 24.9% {wiki_2026}.

items: Says HEA 1004 is meant to "hold hospitals accountable for lower and more transparent pricing, prioritize patients and reduce health care costs" {caucus_hospital_2026}.
In a June 2026 column on hospital pricing and the state's claims database he wrote: "This is meaningful progress, but the work is not finished" {caucus_column_2026}.
The caucus lists his priorities as reducing regulations that hinder workforce growth, a competitive tax code and fiscally conservative state finances {caucus_carbaugh}.
On SEA 88: "This new law helps ensure students are prepared not just for graduation, but for life after high school" {caucus_sea88}.
Was among northeast Indiana legislators announcing the Indiana Utility Regulatory Commission's March 2026 energy affordability investigation, which included Indiana Michigan Power {caucus_iurc}.

on_incumbent: Is the current officeholder. No public statements about his challenger were found. He did not respond to the Journal Gazette's primary questionnaire {jg_d81}.
plans: Says more work remains on health care costs for people with marketplace and other non-direct-employer plans {caucus_hospital_2026}.
endorsements_finance: Wikipedia lists primary endorsements from Donald Trump, Gov. Mike Braun, Americans for Prosperity, the NFIB Indiana PAC and the NRA Political Victory Fund {wiki_2026}. No fundraising figures were verified.
gaps: Campaign finance totals were not checked (state portal not readable).
No statements on data centers, property taxes or the 2025 redistricting vote beyond his recorded votes were found.

candidates.summary: Sharon Wight is a Fort Wayne project manager and former adjunct instructor making her first run for office {jg_d81}. She won the Democratic primary with 81.6% {wiki_2026}.
background: Project manager at an educational technology company that builds websites, apps and communication systems for schools; previously an adjunct instructor at area universities, an academic advisor at Purdue Fort Wayne and briefly a dual-credit instructor at Homestead High School {wight_about}.
Attended Fort Wayne Community Schools and holds two master's degrees {wight_about}. Lives in Fort Wayne {jg_d81}.
Says she has worked as a disability advocate with the League for the Blind and Disabled {jg_d81} and has served as a church secretary since high school {wight_about}.
path_to_ballot: Won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary over Chad Clevidence, 81.6% to 18.4% {wiki_2026}.

items: Named "rapid development in parts of the district while others still need support and maintenance" as the top issue, citing strain on Huntertown's water source {jg_d81}.
Supports directing tax dollars to projects that serve residents rather than corporate developers, and accessible public transit, neighborhoods and buildings {wight_platform}.
Supports public schools, tax funding for education, higher teacher pay and accountability for tax funding {wight_platform}.
Supports a health care system that keeps residents out of bankruptcy, citing Massachusetts as a model {jg_d81}.
Says rental housing should be held to a higher standard {jg_d81}. Opposed 2026's HB 1431 on street camping, saying it "effectively criminalizes homelessness" {wight_platform}.
Says pay has not kept pace with living costs; supports medical and family leave plans and describes herself as "Pro-Union" {wight_platform}.
Lists support for HB 1043, "Data Center Water Regulation" {wight_platform}.
Lists support for bills on straight-ticket voting and same-day voter registration {wight_platform}.
Supports marijuana legalization, abortion rights, same-sex marriage and gender-affirming care {wight_platform}.

on_incumbent: No statements about Carbaugh or his record were found on her website or in the coverage reviewed {wight_site}.
plans: Says her first-year goal is to build relationships with constituents, businesses and colleagues {jg_d81}.
endorsements_finance: No endorsements or fundraising figures were verified.
gaps: Limited news coverage beyond the Journal Gazette primary questionnaire.
HD 83 candidate Wesley Haffenden's campaign site thanks Wight for opposing the proposed southwest Allen County quarry; no statement from Wight herself was found.
